g.text: Before and after: 64 / 32 / 24 / 16 px. Rounded strokes and semantic IDs retained.
Opaque flute body hides the rear workpiece edge; cutter and workpiece no longer form a false X.
A regular 2 x 2 grid follows each projected cube face and meets its edges.
The workspace sector is centered on the base pivot and fully contains the shown end joint.
The loop arrowhead now points away from its incoming shaft at the actual endpoint.
Contact dots are grouped 3 / 2 / 1 in three separate face interiors, away from the seams.
The complete top rim is solid; the dashed sampling section is a separate teal measurement overlay.
The pocket opening remains within the top face; hidden cavity edges no longer cross the front walls.
The open shell has one consistent rim; all interior edges stay inside its visible opening.
The selected loop is a single continuous belt that follows the two visible side faces.
The top profile has one uninterrupted cap; the unintended closing-edge diameter is removed.
The right rotation arrow is inset by two grid units for consistent edge breathing room.
